macrophage.role: The big eater. It engulfs one pathogen at a time, the first each turn free and then 1 Action Point each, and every meal raises antigen presentation, the bridge that switches on the adaptive cells.
macrophage.home: Made in the marrow. It circulates in the blood as a monocyte and enters tissue where it is needed, maturing into a macrophage there. In the game it starts in the Bloodstream and goes wherever you send it.
macrophage.bestAgainst: Viruses and coated bacteria on its own space, and blood-stage malaria. It cannot swallow a worm or a full-strength protozoan. Those are physically too big and must be struck down first.
macrophage.deficiency: Without phagocytes, bacteria and fungi are never cleared, and nothing is ever presented to the adaptive team, so antibodies and killer cells never get their start.
macrophage.fact: A macrophage can engulf tuberculosis bacteria and still fail to kill them. It takes a helper T-cell signal to finish the job, which is why tuberculosis wakes up when helper T-cell counts fall.

neutrophil.role: The first responder. It swarms a site and destroys every living microbe standing there at once. Then it is spent, and the marrow takes four turns to replace it, or two with a primed Helper T-Cell in the Bloodstream.
neutrophil.home: The bloodstream, in enormous numbers: the most abundant white cell in the body, made and replaced by the marrow continuously. In the game it starts in the Bloodstream and moves two steps per Action Point.
neutrophil.bestAgainst: A swarm: bacteria, fungi and viruses standing together on one space. Not worms, not toxins, and nothing hiding inside one of your own cells.
neutrophil.deficiency: Neutropenia, too few neutrophils, as after chemotherapy, leaves the body open to bacterial and fungal infections that are normally stopped within hours.
neutrophil.fact: Neutrophils live only a day or so, and the marrow makes about a hundred billion of them every day. Their NETs are webs of their own DNA, thrown out to trap and kill microbes.

bcell.role: The antibody factory. It produces antibodies of one class at a time; the antibodies then coat or neutralise pathogens of that class wherever they are.
bcell.home: Made in the marrow (the B). In the game it starts in the Bloodstream and produces from wherever it stands, best beside a primed Helper T-Cell, which adds one antibody per action.
bcell.bestAgainst: Anything with an antigen class. Its antibodies tag bacteria, worms and parasites so other cells can attack them, and neutralise viruses and toxins outright. A novel antigen is out of reach until clonal selection finds the one clone that fits it.
bcell.deficiency: No B-cells means no antibodies: bacteria and toxins outside cells run unchecked, and there is nothing for a vaccine to build on. The human version is X-linked agammaglobulinaemia.
bcell.fact: Your body already carries B-cells for antigens it has never met. Finding the one that fits a new pathogen, clonal selection, is why a first response takes days, and why the second time is fast.

tcell.role: The sniper. It kills infected cells, anything hiding inside one of your own cells, from a distance, and it never misses.
tcell.home: Matured in the thymus (the T), then circulating. In the game it starts in the Bloodstream and strikes along its own route or branch within its range: 3 on Training, 2 on Normal and Hard, +1 beside a primed Helper T-Cell.
tcell.bestAgainst: Hidden viruses and the protozoa that live inside cells: Toxoplasma, Chagas, liver-stage malaria, a parasite inside a resident macrophage. Useless against anything out in the open.
tcell.deficiency: Without killer T-cells, a virus that hides inside cells is never cleared, because the infected cell is never destroyed. Reactivating viruses like shingles are what a weakened T-cell system lets through.
tcell.fact: A killer T-cell recognises an infected cell by the fragments of virus that cell displays on its own surface. The cell reports its own infection.

helper.role: The conductor. It kills nothing and takes no attacking action; it licenses other cells by standing with them, but only once it has been primed by antigen presentation.
helper.home: The Bloodstream at the start. Where it stands afterwards is the whole game: beside the B-Cell, beside the Killer T-Cell, beside the Eosinophil, or parked in the blood.
helper.bestAgainst: Nothing directly. Beside the B-Cell: +1 antibody per action. Beside the Killer T-Cell: +1 range. Beside the Eosinophil: +1 step. Standing in the Bloodstream: the Neutrophil returns in 2 turns instead of 4.
helper.deficiency: HIV destroys helper T-cells, and the whole adaptive system collapses with them. That is what AIDS is: not the virus's own damage but the loss of the coordinating layer, leaving the body open to infections it would normally handle easily.
helper.fact: Its three bonuses are real T-helper subsets: Th2 releases IL-5 to recruit eosinophils; Th17 releases IL-17, which drives G-CSF and steps up neutrophil production in the marrow; and direct contact is what licenses a B-cell to make antibodies properly.

nk.role: The innate killer. It needs no antigen and no priming, so it attacks an infected cell at once, but it rolls a die, and hits on a 3 or more.
nk.home: The bloodstream, patrolling on its own. In the game it starts in the Bloodstream, moves two steps per Action Point, and reaches one step around it.
nk.bestAgainst: The same hidden targets as the Killer T-Cell, viruses and protozoa inside your own cells, earlier and less reliably. Its reach is one step; the Killer T-Cell reaches further and never misses.
nk.deficiency: People born without NK cells suffer repeated, severe herpesvirus infections: the viruses that hide inside cells early, before the T-cells are ready.
nk.fact: NK cells kill cells that have stopped showing their identity papers. A virus that hides a cell's surface markers from T-cells makes that cell a target for NK cells instead.

eosinophil.role: The anti-parasite specialist. It strikes a coated worm or parasite for 2 damage, or degranulates for 3, enough to kill a worm outright, at the price of burning the organ it stands in and four turns spent.
eosinophil.home: Made in the marrow, circulating in small numbers and recruited to wherever a parasite is. In the game it starts in the Bloodstream and gains a step beside a primed Helper T-Cell. That is IL-5.
eosinophil.bestAgainst: Worms and large parasites, once antibodies have coated them. It cannot touch an uncoated one, and it is no use against bacteria or viruses.
eosinophil.deficiency: Without eosinophils the body loses its specialist weapon against worms, and some worm infections take longer to clear. Where they are over-active, the same granules turn on the body's own airways. That is asthma and allergy.
eosinophil.fact: Eosinophil granules are indiscriminate poison. That is why parasitic infections cause chronic inflammation and scarring, and why degranulating should feel like a decision rather than a free hit.
